newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World Bank raps Bangladesh for bloated government.
newsitem.headline: World Bank raps Bangladesh for bloated government.

text.p: The World Bank on Wednesday criticised impoverished Bangladesh for its bloated government, accusing it of placing too heavy a burden on the budget and blocking reforms.
In a World Bank global report it said the Bangladesh government has doubled in size since 1971 to almost one million employees.

"Bangladesh needs radical reforms in public administration so that the public is served much better," Pierre Landell-Mills, chief of the World Bank mission in Dhaka, told a news conference on Wednesday at the realese of the World Development Report, 1997.
Apart from the effect on the budget, the report said, expansion of the government had compounded problems of coordination and made regulations more intrusive.
"It has also created vested interests that have blocked efforts at rationalisation and reforms," said the report.
The report says the main issue in South Asia was over-regulation, both a cause and an effect of bloated public sectors.

Landell-Mills said the enormous growth of Non-Government Organisations (NGOs) in Bangladesh and their commendable role were indicators that the private sector could do better than the government in delivering services.
World Bank officials also stressed speedier privatisation of state-owned enterprises to relieve the exchequer from the growing burden of public wages.

"Bangladesh must go resolutely for privatisation. Maybe it's politically difficult but the government is meant for making difficult political decisions," said Owaise Sadaat, a senior World Bank official in Dhaka.
"That South Asia is trapped in the four percent growth rate is the effect of not taking politically difficult decisions by its governments," Sadaat said.
Bangladesh has appointed a private sector entrepreneur as chairman of the Privatisation Board, giving him the status of a junior minister.
The new chairman recently said that 64 state-owned enterprises would be offered for sale by June 30.
The government has announced a big pay hike for public employees which drew the ire of the private sector and international donors.
